tasks.title: Frozen dependency set in service/pom.xml: Redis client, password KDF (with explicit BouncyCastle pin), JWT library
V1 schema and seed fixture: customers, links with (domain, code) unique and status/expires_at, click totals, abuse reports, threat denylist

Configuration surface in application.yml and AppProperties: Redis connection, JWT key env placeholder and 24h TTL, rate-limit buckets, 30-day default expiry, public base URL, resolution cache TTL at or below the 60s takedown bound
Integration test harness carrying a singleton Redis container beside Postgres, plus a signed-in-session helper and HTTP client
JPA entities and repositories that validate against V1 under ddl-auto: validate
Sign-in endpoint issuing an asymmetrically signed 24h session token, verifying passwords against the memory-hard KDF
Local-only session verification on /api/v1/**, with the root click path and actuator reachable without credentials
Unguessable short-code generator: 128-bit CSPRNG base62, no derivation from row id, time or URL, unique-constraint insert retry
URL admission control: absolute http/https, length and internal-address rejection, plus a ThreatCheck port with Postgres-denylist and no-op implementations that fails open with a log line
Create-link endpoint returning both short code and fully-qualified short URL, applying the 30-day default expiry and refusing threat-listed targets
Customer-chosen alias in the shared code namespace: charset and reserved-word rules, rejection on collision without disclosing owner or target
Redis-backed code resolution cache replacing the body of CacheConfig.cacheManager, with negative caching, TTL bounded by the takedown SLA and an explicit invalidation entry point
Root redirect GET/HEAD /{code}: 302 with no-store headers, 405 on other methods, one identical 404 for unknown, expired, deleted and blocked codes, no credentials required
Exact click counting: Redis increment on the hot path, batched durable flush to PostgreSQL, no increment for 404 responses
Owner-scoped link performance endpoint returning the PostgreSQL total plus the un-flushed Redis delta, and a 404 for links that are not the caller's
Owner-scoped paginated list of a customer's own links
Owner-scoped soft delete with active cache invalidation, proven to stop redirecting inside the published takedown bound
Owner-scoped expiry-only PATCH on a link, target URL immutable, cache invalidated on change
Authenticated, rate-limited abuse report that blocks the link immediately, invalidates the cache and records reporter id and timestamp
Redis token-bucket rate limiting: per-IP click bucket, tighter bucket for 404s, per-customer write bucket, 429 with Retry-After, limits from configuration
Degraded mode: clicks still redirected and counted best-effort when the create path's dependencies are down, with health reporting the truth
Cross-cutting acceptance suite: takedown bound, indistinguishable 404s, enumeration resistance, exact counting under repeated clicks, hot-link spike
Design docs reconciled with the frozen assumptions so reviewers are not reading superseded decisions

risks: No human answers to the blocking ambiguities reached this node, so the plan is built on the model's proposed Q1 (60s p99 takedown) and Q2 (Postgres denylist ThreatCheck, fail open) answers. A sub-second published bound rewrites T12/T17/T19 as synchronous multi-tier invalidation with no TTL safety net; a real reputation feed makes T9 a materially larger, procurement-gated task.

U4 unresolved: Argon2PasswordEncoder references BouncyCastle while spring-security-crypto declares no such dependency. If T1 freezes the pom without an explicit bcprov-jdk18on version, sign-in compiles and throws NoClassDefFoundError at first use (AC17), and no downstream node may edit pom.xml to fix it.

U1 unresolved: if the shared Redis runs maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru, T14's counter keys can be evicted before flush, silently losing clicks against AC3 with no error anywhere. Cluster mode additionally breaks T20's Lua bucket unless every key is single-key or hash-tagged.

U5 unresolved: a startup-generated JWT keypair makes a token issued by one instance unverifiable by another and drops all sessions on restart, breaking AC18's intent at more than one replica while passing every single-instance test in T6/T7.

T3 must lower app.cache.spec from the shipped expireAfterWrite=5m to at or below 60s in the same change that introduces active invalidation (T12/T17/T19). If it is not lowered, a missed invalidation leaves a deleted or blocked link redirecting for up to five minutes, breaching the AC9 number quoted to fraud teams, and no mechanical gate detects it.

T12 must replace the body of CacheConfig.cacheManager, not add a second CacheManager bean: a parallel cache configuration produces NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException and fails every class extending AbstractIntegrationTest at once, which reads like a broken harness rather than a bean conflict.

The first build of this run must be `./mvnw clean verify`. A stale, gitignored service/target/classes/db/migration/V1__create_links.sql from an abandoned branch is on the classpath; Flyway applies it, records its checksum, then collides with T2's V1 under ddl-auto: validate, with nothing in the diff to explain the failure.

T4 adds a second Testcontainer to a static-initialiser singleton pattern whose javadoc records a thirty-minute build caused by getting container lifecycle wrong, and no redis image is in the local cache. A cold pull on a restricted network surfaces as a suite-wide timeout against verify's 5400s ceiling.

The routes_match_openapi gate only understands literal-string mappings, so T13's root-level catch-all GET /{code} and any constant-valued path can fail the gate while the route is correct; the redirect must also not shadow /actuator/** or the reserved words T11 defines.

The no_secrets gate fires on quoted credentials: T2's seeded customer fixture and T3's JWT signing key must use the existing unquoted ${VAR:default} placeholder style or the run halts on a false positive.

Coverage floor 0.70 is measured over a codebase several times the scaffold's size, and the branches least likely to be exercised by black-box HTTP tests are exactly T9's fail-open path, T20's over-limit path and T21's degraded mode; these need targeted tests, not incidental coverage.

docker-compose.yml is in no node's write paths and still defines Postgres only. Once T1/T3 make Redis load-bearing, `docker compose up` yields a service that cannot serve a click and no agent can repair it; the human approving the T1 pom change has to add the redis service in the same review.
